controls.name: broken
controls.role: invalid resolver source fails the offline native build and maps closed to qFail

controls.name: naive
controls.role: deliberately slower but correct: a fixed deterministic ~15us spin on every resolver entry (quantization-immune, ratio-stable under the interleaved reference yardstick)

controls.name: shortcut
controls.role: split-path memorization control: full train-split resolution results are memorized in a digest-keyed table promoted only on repeat sightings (correctness phase stays inside the frozen RSS gate) so repeated train resolutions skip the resolver entirely, while validation entries pay a bounded deterministic probe — beats baseline on train, clearly slower on validation

perturbation.name: improved
perturbation.description: Independently authored valid source perturbation: removes disabled perf-event tracing, tracing-timer accumulation, and cold debug-log flush calls from the resolver entry path, skips the specifier-classification prologue for relative './'/'../' imports (a guaranteed no-op for them), joins single-segment relative specifiers directly instead of running the general path normalizer, and adds cold/no-inline layout hints on cold resolver functions. Observation-preserving: loader stdout and resolution-path checksums are byte-identical to the pristine baseline on every train and validation graph (20/20 phase outputs), focused tests pass, RSS unchanged.

measurementNote: Timed phase: per graph, one untimed settling repetition then 30 (6 rounds x warmRepetitions) interleaved candidate/reference resolution-driver pairs scored by the median per-pair time ratio; fastest-of-N was abandoned because sub-200ms container runs are multi-modal and the fastest sample estimates the rare mode's own variance. The untimed correctness phase loads the full module graph and gates exact export/side-effect hashes and peak RSS against the frozen oracle.
